author: reek
body: `sym` and `bp-add` were the last two commands that prompted for something and consumed nothing. Both had WORKING IMPLEMENTATIONS WITH NO CALLER: `debug-sym-lookup` and `bp-add-symbolic` were defined in `DevDebugger` and reached from nowhere, while the menu advertised both. The line each prompted for fell through to the address evaluator and moved the cursor.

author: reek
body: So this is a wiring test and it is driven entirely through `handle-console-input`, for the same reason `debug-expr` and `dev-mem-cmd` are: calling the helpers directly would pass against the old arms too.

author: reek
body: A NAME IS NOT AN EXPRESSION, and that is the reading this test exists to pin. The write value added earlier goes through `ExprEval`; these two must not. `parse-expr` handed to an evaluator answers "unknown name" for something that was never meant to be one, and the failure would look like a broken symbol table rather than a misrouted line.

author: reek
body: THE INDEX IS POPULATED ON PURPOSE. `dev-console-init` starts with `empty-source-index` -- the real console fills it after boot -- and against an empty index every query answers "No symbols matching", so the hit and the miss would be the same line and neither would mean anything. The test seeds `index-full-dev-surface`, which is the same canned surface the console indexes, so `parse` finds definitions and `zzz-no-such-symbol` does not.

author: reek
body: The breakpoint line answers "Symbol not found: zzz-no-such-function", and that string is produced by `bp-add-symbolic` and by nothing else -- had the line fallen through to the evaluator it would read `expr: unknown name zzz-no-such-function` -- so it still proves the line was ROUTED to the symbolic path. Since main 11552 fixed `map1-find` it proves more than that: the map really is found and `map1-find-by-name` really is walked, which this paragraph used to say no test here could do.

author: reek
body: The cursor readings are the discriminating ones. After each name is consumed, `$` reports where the cursor really is: if a name had fallen through to the evaluator, the cursor would have moved or the status would carry an expression error. `$` answering the address the FIRST expression set is what proves the two names went somewhere else entirely.
